quest.title: Where the Boat of Consciousness Lies
quest.description: Although you have saved Lesser Lord Kusanali, there is no time to celebrate or rest, for there is a nascent god to stop and Irminsul to save... Now, the fate of Teyvat is in your hands.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1150, Primogem x30, Mora x45525, Memory of Flourishing Green x1, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

chapter.title: Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises

talks.objective: Wait until 16:00 and find Nahida in the Sanctuary of Surasthana

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How's it going, Nahida?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I'm done with the parts that needed my involvement to complete.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Although it's my first time working with the Akasha like this, its internal structure and operation procedures are easy for me to understand. Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's design is truly brilliant.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Oh, also, this is for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What's this little floaty thingy?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It's a small device I put together just now. You can think of it as an upgraded Akasha Terminal.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: You may not need it right now, but it should be helpful in certain situations.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait! This thing has the same characteristics as Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're both small things that float...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* All the things that make Paimon special got copied... When Paimon appears with the Traveler from now on, people won't remember Paimon because she isn't unique anymore...

choices.text: Are you actually upset...?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It's alright, Paimon. It can't replace you.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #It's only a flying device, but you're {NICKNAME}'s irreplaceable friend.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Waah, you're so good at comforting people, Nahida. If only {NICKNAME} was as smart as you...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hm? I was simply telling you what I feel to be the truth. I wasn't trying to comfort you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nahida, you're a natural at this! What you just said made Paimon even happier!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: By the way, there's something I need to confess...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Even though I'm the archon and in control of myself again, I'm not very good at fighting...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You may have heard that an archon's power is derived from their people's faith. However, I'm not as well-loved as Greater Lord Rukkhadevata.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: If we get into a situation where combat is our only option, I'll have to count on you, and I'll do my best to provide support.

choices.text: Don't worry.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I'm glad I can rely on you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, so the God of Wisdom isn't good at fighting. That actually sounds about right.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I've located where the false god is. Time is of the essence, so let's skip to it.

choices.text: Fighting is my forte.
It looks completely different from you!

talks.objective: Talk to Nahida once you have made your preparations
Go through the passage and reach The Balladeer

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is this place? Is this really the way we need to go?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... Who woulda thought there'd be a place like this hidden right slap bang in the middle of the city!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The sages wanted to realize their god creation plan without being discovered. The safest and most convenient way would be to build within the Akademiya itself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, that's true. They were already hiding one god, so why not two?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Judging from the structure here, the project is a huge undertaking. The sages really saw the god creation plan as their ultimate goal.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But this place doesn't seem like it could have been constructed by the Akademiya alone...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The Fatui under The Doctor sure didn't hold back — they provided a lot of technological support.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's to help one of their own Harbingers become a god, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, or else they wouldn't have been that generous!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Is that it, though? I've always felt that this "Doctor" is different from the Akademiya sages. He doesn't seem to share their sense of urgency...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Instead of being interested in the end product, it's like he's enjoying the experimental process.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... The Fatui Harbingers are all such weirdos, so The Doctor being weird is actually normal.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: So... this Fatui that they're trying to turn into a god... is called "The Balladeer"?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: We had previously come into contact with his consciousness. He harbors particularly strong obsessions...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: One is the desire for a Gnosis, since he was created to be the vessel for one.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The other obsession is probably related to his past. I can't quite explain it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon knows that he was a prototype puppet for the Raiden Shogun before he became a Fatui Harbinger...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's why he wants a Gnosis so badly. There's no way he'd willingly be a test subject, not with that temper and ego of his.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It sounds like you know The Balladeer quite well.

choices.text: We've had a few encounters...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I see. Tell me more about him and what he's like...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The more we know now, the better we can plan for and react to any future situation.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Nahida everything you know about The Balladeer...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Ah... I see. How fascinating.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Alright, time to go. Let's get through here and meet him in person.

choices.text: But none of them were pleasant.

talks.objective: Go through the passage and reach The Balladeer

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Looking at its operational status, we must prepare for the worst. The god they wanted to create... is likely close to completion, or already completed.

choices.text: That's not a surprise...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh no, what should we do... Paimon can't imagine how hard it would be to fight against a Fatui Harbinger with a Gnosis...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Are you nervous, Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you really want to know... of course Paimon's nervous! Aren't you too, Nahida?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yes, I am. This is probably the first time I'm faced with a calamity of this degree since my birth.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I feel not just nervous, but curious as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Curious...? Curious about what?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Curious about our fate.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: To me, everything we perceive in this world, everything we learn, and everything that happens to us is considered knowledge.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: And if it's a form of knowledge, then it can be understood.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: However, only fate is about that which has yet to occur, so it has always drawn my curiosity.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: So to me, "fate" is the ultimate knowledge.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: That's also why I love observing humans and all the things that happen to them. It all brings me great satisfaction.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: And now, at long last, I'm not just an observer anymore.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I will personally experience my own fate, with you by my side. Hehe, isn't this such a wonderfully exciting thing?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, so that's what you mean! Paimon thinks she understands what you're feeling.

choices.text: I'm also looking forward to it.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Agreed! Okay, let's continue on. I can sense "his" aura from here...

choices.text: We won't lose.
I've already seen him control the weather.

talks.objective: Go to where The Balladeer is

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This imposing aura... It really feels like a god's...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: A body that capitalizes on The Balladeer's original construction as a mechanical puppet, with the Gnosis serving as a constant power supply...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: How much effort and resources did the sages put into this...?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: From a purely technological perspective, it's a commendable achievement indeed. It's no exaggeration to say this is the culmination of human wisdom.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You sure are something, dishing out compliments at a time like this...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But I don't think he's reached the spiritual height of a god.

choices.text: So he's still the same, old Balladeer on the inside.

response.speaker: Everlasting Lord of Arcane Wisdom
response.text: Strife is engraved upon every god and every Gnosis brought forth into this world.

response.speaker: Everlasting Lord of Arcane Wisdom
response.text: Can you feel it? The exhilaration of such power, and the thrill of anticipation for our contention...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nahida wouldn't feel the same things as you!

response.speaker: Everlasting Lord of Arcane Wisdom
response.text: Do you not realize... that you are interrupting a conversation between gods? Lowly creature, know your place!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Still the same Balladeer we know...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The strife engraved upon a Gnosis... You're talking about the Archon War.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Teyvat's current peace was not easily won. I didn't personally participate in the Archon War, but the way I see it...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: All those losses were meaningless, driven by the demands of the "laws." There's no point in bringing it up again.

response.speaker: Everlasting Lord of Arcane Wisdom
response.text: Hehehe, is that so? Yet I am deeply disappointed that I was never allowed the fortuity to personally participate in the Archon War.

response.speaker: Everlasting Lord of Arcane Wisdom
response.text: This is a first — encountering a god in this world who does not crave power.

response.speaker: Everlasting Lord of Arcane Wisdom
response.text: No wonder your own people have abandoned you, God of Wisdom.

choices.text: But from now on...

response.speaker: Everlasting Lord of Arcane Wisdom
response.text: Hmph. Your judgment is as your existence: unsubstantial.

response.speaker: Everlasting Lord of Arcane Wisdom
response.text: This is where everything ends, Buer, the God of Wisdom.

response.speaker: Everlasting Lord of Arcane Wisdom
response.text: You should know that wisdom cannot solve every problem. Like now, where your only option is to face me in combat.

response.speaker: Everlasting Lord of Arcane Wisdom
response.text: Come...

response.speaker: Everlasting Lord of Arcane Wisdom
response.text: Let us reenact a scene of the Archon War. Come and inaugurate my birth as a god.

choices.text: Nahida's followers will only continue to increase in number.
I'm not sure if that's a good or bad thing...

talks.objective: Defeat the Everlasting Lord of Arcane Wisdom
Defeat the Everlasting Lord of Arcane Wisdom
Enter Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's last memory

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, this sure seems very different from what Paimon imagined... Shouldn't Irminsul be in this realm of consciousness?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes, that is our destination, but I didn't expect the remaining consciousness of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata to be as polluted as this.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Polluted?

choices.text: Surely not...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Forbidden knowledge? Hmm, it seems you know about a concept that even I don't completely understand. Could you tell me what you know?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Nahida all about what you had learned in the desert.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Your inference seems logical enough...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Forbidden knowledge once polluted the desert thousands of years ago, but was successfully repelled thanks to King Deshret's self-sacrifice and Greater Lord Rukkhadevata nearly exhausting her power.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Then a second instance of forbidden knowledge pollution occurred during the Khaenri'ah cataclysm five hundred years ago.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But I'm afraid it is much more serious this time, with Irminsul itself already in danger.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So if we're in the remaining consciousness of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, and it's also been affected by forbidden knowledge pollution, then does that mean, in order to save us, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yes, it's very possible that she sacrificed her life in the fight against forbidden knowledge.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: She didn't completely eradicate forbidden knowledge, but if it weren't for her actions, the pollution would have been far more rampant over these past five hundred years.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The way that everyone, including me, has forgotten everything about forbidden knowledge may very well be due to her restoration of Irminsul.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, do you feel sad, Nahida?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I'm just sharing her pain... The pollution of her consciousness here is severe. There is madness, chaos, and pain all around us.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Did she fight to resist the forbidden knowledge pollution in such terrible conditions, all the way up till her last breath...?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: She even used her last remnant of lucid consciousness to leave a clue for us to follow...

choices.text: By "clue," you mean...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yes, her words were distorted by forbidden knowledge, so that's all we could hear.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But now we have a chance to find the answer to this mystery.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: We can cross the polluted consciousness until we've found the right path to meet with her lucid consciousness.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: And then... we'll let Greater Lord Rukkhadevata tell us the truth in person.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I hope we can use that truth to save everybody.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Each of us need to be mindful of the state of our own consciousness while we are here.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Even with the Gnosis' protection, we must always keep a clear mind. Otherwise, we could go mad at any moment.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eek! That's so scary!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Don't worry, it should be easy enough for you to keep that mind of yours clear, Paimon. Let's go.

choices.text: The words, "...World... Forget me..."?
It must be due to forbidden knowledge.

talks.objective: Leave this place using the Boat of Consciousness

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We changed direction. Are we still going the right way, Nahida?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm. Judging from the current route, the Boat of Consciousness will soon take us out of here.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: We'll be arriving at our destination soon. How are you feeling? Are your minds still intact?

choices.text: Some strange thoughts came from time to time...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, but everything's been completely normal for Paimon.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hopefully, there won't be any more interruptions. This time, we should be able to meet Greater Lord Rukkhadevata.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you saying you've never met Greater Lord Rukkhadevata before?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: No, it seems that my birth and her death took place at the same time.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Otherwise, I think she would have given me a little more guidance, and I could have done a better job.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, you've done a great job, Nahida! Let's get out of this creepy place and go meet her!

choices.text: But I seem to be okay now.

talks.objective: Reach the Irminsul from the past
Find the remaining consciousness of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Well, this is the place.

choices.text: Yes...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... we're here to find Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But the one standing over there is...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Is that... me...? She looks exactly... like me...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Are you... Greater Lord Rukkhadevata?

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: Yes, that's me. Are you surprised by my appearance?

choices.text: I can't believe my eyes...

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: Irminsul and the surrounding lands have been reproduced here as they were years ago, but this is just a realm of consciousness.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: We are manifestations of the same nature, hence why we would appear exactly the same.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hmm? We're... of the same nature? Why?

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: Because you are me, and I am you.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: You are me in the new samsara.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The new samsara...

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: As Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, I'm the avatar of Irminsul, and you are the purest branch snapped from Irminsul.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: Imagine it this way... Even if a tree dies, its branches will eventually take root and grow, continuing the tree's life in another form.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: I'm merely the remaining consciousness of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata. The real me has presumably died a long time ago.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: Hmm... Judging from your appearance, I've probably been dead for five hundred years...

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: But you're finally here, my new "self" in this samsara.

choices.text: So this is the connection between you two...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: If this is true, then am I... going to be a great archon like you someday?

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: Though we share the same nature, our fates are bound to be different. All things have their own fate.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: When a branch grows into a mature tree, it won't be the same as the original tree.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: That's why fate is the ultimate knowledge, isn't it?

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: That's a great insight. Yes, very good.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: It's also precisely why you won't become like me...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Really...

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: But perhaps, you may become an even greater archon than I.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: I already see a determination in you that I didn't possess in my time, and the future that it leads you to will be yours alone.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: Along with the blessings from your past experiences.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: Don't worry. The growth of wisdom is like that of a plant — you only need to wait quietly for the flower to bloom.

choices.text: I have faith in Nahida, too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come to think of it, the sages never had the faintest inkling of the meaning of wisdom...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Thank you... Nothing makes me happier than discovering that the archon I always admired was in fact myself in another fate.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It's so nice to speak with you, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata. I've always wanted to meet you...

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: The feeling is mutual. From the moment I snapped the branch off Irminsul and created you, I've also looked forward to talking with you.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Could you tell me... why you wanted to create me? And what exactly happened when you died...

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: Ah, I see. You're here seeking answers, right?

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: Everything that day, even the sky itself, changed into a color like this...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I knew it... the Khaenri'ah cataclysm.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: At that time, The Seven were all summoned to the nation of Khaenri'ah, except for me. I had a more important task to attend to...

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: I had to protect Irminsul.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: The disaster occurred together with the pollution of forbidden knowledge. At that very moment, with my consciousness connected to Irminsul, I sensed something was wrong.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: The pain started to torment my mind. By the time I reached Irminsul, it was already displaying signs of corruption.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: Had I not repelled the pollution of forbidden knowledge with King Deshret thousands of years ago, I might have felt even more hopeless and lost.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: So what exactly is... forbidden knowledge?

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: It's a kind of knowledge that doesn't belong to this world, and a form of "truth" that can't be understood.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: It came from the very bottom of the Abyss. Even I could never understand it.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: The world is constantly rejecting it, leading to all kinds of bad phenomena.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: If we allow forbidden knowledge to pollute Irminsul, I'm afraid the entirety of Teyvat could fall apart.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So there's knowledge that even the God of Wisdom can't understand...

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: At that time, I knew I couldn't repel the forbidden knowledge with my strength alone.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: Which is why I created a device that compiled human wisdom, and named it "the Akasha."

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It's truly the world's most amazing invention.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: Hehe... Thank you. For a long time, I thought dreams were the fruit of human wisdom.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: Though it was selfish to do so, I borrowed people's dreams using the Akasha. Then I compiled their wisdom and all of my own power...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, did it work?

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: Thanks to the wisdom of the people of Sumeru, almost all the forbidden knowledge was cleared from Irminsul.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: But... things didn't go as smoothly as I thought. I had a terrible headache, which gave me an uneasy feeling...

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: And then, I remembered that my consciousness was also connected with Irminsul. It brought me knowledge and wisdom, but vile corruption as well.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: From the very beginning, my existence had been polluted by the forbidden knowledge.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh no... How could that happen...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I've experienced that pain in your consciousness. It must've been a horrible experience.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: Yes, but my feelings weren't important. The important thing was that...

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: Even if I died, my existence and everything related to me would continue to exist in Irminsul as memories and knowledge, meaning that the forbidden knowledge couldn't ever be permanently eradicated.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: And... there's no way for me to eliminate myself. It would be a sort of paradox.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: So, I took the purest branch of Irminsul as my incarnation in the next samsara, and left a trail of clues...

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: All in hopes that you would come here and remove me and my pollution from Irminsul forever.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...W—Wait. No... I can't!

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: Hehe, so you realized what that implies? You are very smart, indeed.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: Irminsul has all the knowledge and memories of this world. And as you've realized just now...

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: Removing me from Irminsul means... I essentially will never have existed in this world.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: But... this is the only way to save Irminsul.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: People love you so much and... and they've missed you so much over the past five hundred years. I... I am exactly the same. So how...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: How can we just... forget you like this?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Is there really no other way? There must be something else I can do!

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: You're the God of Wisdom, Buer. You should know that there is no other way.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But this... this is so... cruel. I don't want to forget you!

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: No need to feel so sad, Buer. As someone who delights in wisdom, you should feel joy at finally finding the answer.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: These are the words in their entirety... the answer you've been seeking all along.

response.speaker: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata
response.text: "Let the world completely forget me."

choices.text: She will definitely become a great archon.
Lesser Lord Kusanali and Greater Lord Rukkhadevata...
The two of you look almost exactly the same...
It's the same place from my memories.
Nahida?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #Ah, {NICKNAME}, I—I'm all right. I'm just a little confused...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What are you confused about?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: We've just saved the world, right?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: So why... why am I crying?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I don't know where this feeling inside of me is coming from, but I feel very sad...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Do you still remember... what happened just now?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Just now? We used the power of two Gnoses to successfully connect with the Irminsul consciousness from five hundred years ago...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Then, we removed the remaining pollution from Irminsul...

choices.text: (She's forgotten her...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Yeah, what's wrong? {NICKNAME}, weren't you there just now?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Paimon doesn't seem to remember either. Has everybody really forgotten Greater Lord Rukkhadevata?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Should I... tell them the truth?)
*Buzzing*

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (What's that sound...? I feel... super... sleepy...)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #Huh, that sound... {NICKNAME}? Paimon?

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: I've been waiting here far too long... But finally, I have the chance to be alone with you. All the precious time I wasted has finally paid off.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The Doctor... What have you done!?

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Just a type of sound wave that can quickly put defenseless people into a dream. As I expected... it doesn't have any effect on gods.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: This is the only thing of interest I found among the sages' research. I thought I'd take it for a little spin.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Don't worry. I know you would never forgive me if I actually killed them.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: I'm here to negotiate with you. Naturally, I won't do anything dangerous that could potentially damage our relationship.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Negotiate with me? I heard you had already left Sumeru. Why are you here again now?

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: "I" left Sumeru, but "I" also stayed in Sumeru.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Even the God of Wisdom is restricted by the habits of cognition. How disappointing.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You mean... there are many different versions of you in this world?

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: An astute guess.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Even the same individual will have different cognitions at different ages.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: A long time ago, I made a major decision in hopes of preserving all my perspectives of how I observed the world.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Observation is the first step of any experiment, but observing the current world doesn't satisfy me. It lacks an important dimension — that of time.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: So I saved "segments" of all my ages, and made them into independent individuals...

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: That's all there is to it. Indulge me, how does the God of Wisdom find my method of seeking knowledge?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It's an insult to the very concept of life.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Life inherently has many rules and restrictions, each with its own significance and reason to exist. They can't be broken on a whim.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Hehehehe... Good. Amazing, even.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Indeed. It's difficult for humans... to make peace with themselves, not to mention oneself from a different period.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Since you were in the Akademiya, why wait until now to show up? You could very well have stopped us and helped that "fake god."

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Simple, let me ask you this: Would any staff member ever help the subject in the middle of an experiment?

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: It was my experiment, so why should I interfere with the results?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...The Akademiya saw the plan to create a god as their ultimate goal, yet you only saw it as an ordinary experiment...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Y—You really are crazy... If the experiment succeeded, you would have had a new god on your hands. How would you have faced your own god then?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Would you still take the same stance? Would you still hold the same view of yourself?

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: I'm first and foremost a scholar. These results should be left to the judgment of the hypothetical "me" confronted with that outcome. But you're right, and that's exactly why I'm disappointed with the conclusion of this experiment.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: As an individual, you don't have any sense of belonging... And you seem to have even fewer convictions than a typical scholar.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Oh, no. I certainly have my own convictions. They just don't fit your standards, that's all.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: All right, that's enough conversation for today. The experiment is over and it's time to tidy up the equipment and reclaim any useful materials.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: For example... the Gnosis.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Lesser Lord Kusanali, you're an intelligent archon. I'm sure you understand the disparity in our combat abilities at this time... Besides, you have no way to use that Electro Gnosis in battle.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Didn't you say you were here to negotiate with me? Somehow it's starting to seem like you intend to take it by force now.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Hahaha... I'm merely stating a fact.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: After all, I'm also a scholar. Naturally, I hope to show proper respect and dignity to the God of Wisdom.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Your hypocrisy is built on absolute confidence.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I understand your scheme, but...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...What if I were to destroy the Gnosis now, and awaken the Heavenly Principles?

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Awaken... the heavenly principles?

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Do you think that's really possible?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The Heavenly Principles have been silent for many years, but the Gnoses are symbols of their control over Teyvat and all the laws...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Will the destruction of a Gnosis attract the attention of the Heavenly Principles? And if so... how do the Fatui plan to deal with the consequences?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Do you dare... to gamble such a possibility with me?

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Hmph, "gamble"? How surprising.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: I thought you would show evidence or use rigorous reasoning to prove your point... The word "gamble" is the last thing I expected to hear from the God of Wisdom.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: But this is a clever move. You must have seen through me when I first captured your consciousness.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: As a scholar, I respect all possibilities. This has always been my principle and is an essential trait as an experimenter.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Indeed, I can't ignore this possibility. So tell me then, what are your conditions?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: This foreign Gnosis will only lead to disaster if it stays in Sumeru...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But this Electro Gnosis is the prize I obtained after defeating one of your fellow Harbingers.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Now, as the one who initiated this cascade of events, shouldn't you pay the corresponding price?

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Price? Interesting. What price would you have me pay?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...How about erasing all your other segments?

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Hahaha... So this is how you wish to restrict me, the most threatening opponent of the Nation of Wisdom. What you request of me is like plucking out the eyes I have placed in the dimension of time.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Segments are extraordinarily difficult to make. They require extremely rare resources and enormous amounts of time and effort. Requiring me to destroy them all here and now... Bravo, a suitably wise decision on your part.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Yes, how very interesting... Can I assume that you have long been wary of me?

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Among all the versions of me, this segment you see now is the most selfish. If it weren't me, your idea wouldn't have worked.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: What did you see when you were imprisoned? You were observing me, and that's how you know I've long grown tired of their doubts and endless arguments.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Like you said, it's difficult to make peace with yourself.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Being as smart as you are, have you managed to do that?

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: I see. If you think all those versions of me are worth a Gnosis... Then, deal.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You sure didn't hesitate much. Is the relationship between all the versions of you really that bad?

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: I don't think there's any need to dwell on that. The surplus versions of me can be exchanged for a Gnosis. Do you think anyone can offer themselves at a higher price?

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Besides, with my abilities, it's only a matter of time until I find better "perspectives." Perhaps it's best to say... you're just temporarily ahead.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: But what I'd like to know is, how can you be sure that I've really erased them?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I can see your remaining honesty...

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: ...Hmph.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Well? Have you confirmed that it's complete?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...Here, take it.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The future of Sumeru City will be in my hands alone. I will shut down the Akasha and let curiosity and the thirst for knowledge drive the realm of academics once again...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: There won't be any further gaps for you to exploit.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: It truly pains me that my academic achievements have never been appreciated in my homeland. Of course, I have no interest in being rejected by this city for a third time.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Another chess piece... And where is your Dendro Gnosis?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...Don't be greedy, Harbinger of Snezhnaya.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: No, this is a different transaction. If you intend to turn off the Akasha anyway, then there's no further use for the Gnosis of Sumeru, is there?

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Besides, isn't it the archon's duty to deliver what's desired of the seeker?

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Oh? Judging from your expression, you don't seem to find the idea very agreeable. Then let's think of it this way... Since you're the God of Wisdom, how about I exchange some knowledge with you?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: People exchanging knowledge with the God of Wisdom is the stuff of legends, yet here you wish to exchange knowledge for the God of Wisdom's property...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Arrogant as that is, it has piqued my interest.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Let me ask you... Have you in all your mighty knowledge ever heard the rumor that "the skies of Teyvat are fake"?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...Huh?

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: That's the secret hidden by Irminsul concerning the "truth" of this world...

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Once I finish telling you about this, it will be time for me to say goodbye.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: With negotiations, we've all gotten what we wanted. I'm very glad I got to meet you like this.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Your arrogance may know no bounds, and convictions may mean nothing to you, but I'll still listen to what you have to say.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Secrets and dark truths flow to the mind of the wise. Then... everything falls silent.

choices.text: (Did I manage to remember because I'm not from this world?)
Don't tell me...
...Are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Wait for... together... Okay... Wake... up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you awake? Collei says it's time for breakfast. C'mon, get up!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good morning, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good morning! How're you feeling today?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Pretty good.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good to hear. It looks like we've recovered pretty well. Not even Tighnari can stop us from going out now, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's right.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (On that day, we lost consciousness in battle... When we woke up, we found ourselves in Gandharva Ville, and Tighnari and Collei were looking after us.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I heard that it was Cyno who brought us here. Tighnari complained that Cyno was always sending people to him, but he has taken great care of us.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (After completely exhausting ourselves, we had a good rest here. After a few days, we finally recovered enough to be able to go back out.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (From what Tighnari and Collei have said, the Akasha has been turned off completely, and the people of Sumeru will no longer rely on it.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Such a big change will certainly affect people's lives... But it will definitely be a good thing.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C'mon, Traveler! Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Observe the unconscious guards...
dialogues.text: (Someone has knocked these two guards out and removed their Akasha Terminals not long ago. No one seems to have noticed them yet.)

dialogues.speaker: Observe the unconscious guards...
dialogues.text: (If they were escorting someone before being knocked out, that person must've escaped.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Today's the big day! Let's go to the Grand Bazaar and see how the celebration's coming along.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Several days later...

dialogues.speaker: Viraf
dialogues.text: The blond-haired Traveler? How did you come out from the Sanctuary of Surasthana? It's normally forbidden to enter that place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, sorry, we don't know the rules here...

dialogues.speaker: Viraf
dialogues.text: It's fine, just pay more attention next time. Anyway, I'm looking for Grand Sage Azar. Have you seen him?

dialogues.speaker: Viraf
dialogues.text: The more I think about it, the more I believe there's something fishy about Alhaitham's return. I need to let the Grand Sage know somehow...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're finally starting to put two and two together...

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Hey, it's you guys! How did your plan go? Are you here for Nilou?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It went really well! And yeah, where's Nilou?

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Great to hear! Nilou's already returned to the Grand Bazaar. Just now, a crowd of Akademiya students came by to ask Nilou for her signature. I've never seen her run away so fast!

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: To think the Akademiya wants to ban artistic performances... Hehe, I think their students would be the first to disagree.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Eh? How did you find the time to walk around? Did you manage to rescue Lesser Lord Kusanali?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We did! She's handling some Akasha stuff right now.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: That's great, haha. Just now, Dehya went to find Asfand, the senior consultant of the Corps of Thirty, and explained everything to him.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: In response, Asfand said, "Why didn't you tell me earlier. If it was to rescue the Dendro Archon, we would've helped as well," hahaha...

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: I didn't know we could have even counted the city guards of the Corps of Thirty among our potential reinforcements. It looks like we were a bit too conservative with our plan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #We might as well prepare for a fight, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: When we're done, we can take a walk around. After all, we missed out on a lot of stuff when we were locked up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The pattern on the ground seems to be all messed up... Let's go around and see if there's a way to fix it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It seems to have stopped. Let's continue.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are we... in the air? And why is there a huge boat!?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: That's the Boat of Consciousness, which symbolizes reason here. Its course is the direction our consciousness is traveling towards.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: If we lose control over our consciousness, we will fall into madness... So let's make sure the boat stays on course.
